consumer: game::handle_action's ACTION_MOVE_* dispatch, which performs the move via avatar_action::move(u,m,dest_delta) and lets the turn loop own the tick
scope: not applicable (an action, not a query) — the move is driven through the engine's own active input-dispatch site for the registered planar movement action
decisive_source: src/handle_action.cpp::game::handle_action (ACTION_MOVE_*) — its body calls avatar_action::move(u,m,dest_delta) and on success leaves the turn loop to consume the moves/tick, the way a keypress would
divergence: A wall (or other impassable terrain) one tile east: a correct action-fidelity path leaves the avatar in place and costs no turn, whereas a shortcut that writes the position/snapshot directly would 'move' the avatar east through the wall and/or fail to debit moves
